newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Forecasts mixed for Trencor's H1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Forecasts mixed for Trencor's H1 earnings.

text.p: South African transport and container firm Trencor Ltd is likely to report fairly good results for the six months to-end December 31, but the continuing rand surge could slow its second half profits, analysts said on Friday.
Analysts polled by Reuters varied widely on the amount by which Trencor could raise its earnings when it reports its first half results on Tuesday.
Some even forcast a flat first half.
"Well their results may be up a little bit, but overall I think they will not be much of a difference from the previous half," said one analyst, who did not want to be named.

However, other analysts said the depreciation of the rand last year could put a sparkle in Trencor's earnings since about 80 percent of profits came from the firm's container division Textainer which is mostly foreign currency-based.
"They (Trencor) are a company which is positively favoured by the weakness in the rand," one analyst said, adding the second half could take a pounding if the current persistent rand climb continued.
"The outlook for the future is good, but at the moment with the rand continuing to strengthen things could be tough for their second half," he added.
Overall the poll showed analysts expected Trencor's earnings to be between a flat 51.9 and 72 cents, with a consensus for the six-month period at 60.3.
Analysts forecast a dividend of between a flat 12 cents a share to 14 cents.
